text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sums spent by the government over the last four years for health, education and sports disarm the opposition in a parliament budget debate.
- Cypriot contractors boycott government projects to protest against the inclusion of foreign companies in tenders.
- A proposal for the deployment of a multinational force in Cyprus is being discussed, says the government.
- Defence spending for 1997 is estimated at 5.8 percent of the gross domestic product, says defence expert.
- The Glafcos Clerides government has isolated Cyprus internationally with its position on the Cyprus problem, says communist Akel party leader Demetris Christofias.
- Party candidates for the presidential elections with tough conditions. Former president and leader of the centre-right Diko party Spyros Kyprianou rejects Akel's terms for dialogue and cooperation.
- Right-wing Disy party president Yiannakis Matsis supports party elections to renew the party leadership.
